briefing.headline: Software carve-outs and niche launches reshape insurance
briefing.teaser: Big software sale talks, specialist cover launches, and cyber shutdown worries
briefing.whatsHappening: The new stories are a mix of dealmaking and narrow, targeted product launches. DXC Technology is reported to be in talks to sell its insurance software unit to Eldridge Industries for $2.4 bn, and smaller buyers are picking up education, health data and cyber-training businesses. At the same time, specialty cover is being sliced ever thinner, with new programs for community association liability, artisan contractors and US mid-market professions, plus fresh capacity added to a reinsurance treaty portfolio. Two disclosed rounds, including $27 million for Slingshot Insurance, total about $54 million, while Aviva and insureMO took embedded insurance across Europe and Brown & Brown unveiled an in-house intelligence platform.
briefing.whyItMatters: Software owners are being reshuffled just as carriers and brokers build their own data tools, so who controls the core systems may matter more over the next year. Insurance M&A is reported down 27% in the third quarter, so a large software deal would stand out against a slower market. Also watch cyber brokers: flaws that could trigger shutdown coverage claims test how well policies handle outages, and the chief executive of Chubb is already calling for the industry to take on AI liability.
